# Standard library reference

<!-- Generated by `tern docs`. Do not edit by hand: run `tools/gen-docs.sh`. -->

Arity notation: `push(value)` takes one argument, `sort([comparator])` takes
an optional one, `println(...)` is variadic. Method signatures omit the
receiver, so `list.push(value)` is written `push(value)` under `list`.

## Globals

| Name | Signature | Notes |
| ---- | --------- | ----- |
| `abs` | `abs(arg)` | Absolute value. |
| `assert` | `assert(arg, [arg])` | Throws unless the condition is truthy. |
| `bool` | `bool(arg)` | Converts a value to a boolean. |
| `chr` | `chr(arg)` | Unicode code point to string. |
| `copy` | `copy(arg)` | Shallow copy of a list or map. |
| `eprint` | `eprint(...)` | Writes its arguments to stderr. |
| `error` | `error(arg)` | Raises an error. |
| `float` | `float(arg)` | Converts a value to a floating point number. |
| `has` | `has(arg, arg)` | True when the map contains the key. |
| `input` | `input([arg])` | Reads one line from stdin. |
| `int` | `int(arg, [arg])` | Converts a value to an integer. |
| `keys` | `keys(arg)` | Keys of a map. |
| `len` | `len(arg)` | Number of items in a string, list, map or range. |
| `max` | `max(arg, ...)` | Largest argument. |
| `min` | `min(arg, ...)` | Smallest argument. |
| `ord` | `ord(arg)` | First character of a string as a code point. |
| `panic` | `panic([arg])` | Aborts the script with a panic error. |
| `print` | `print(...)` | Writes its arguments to stdout without a trailing newline. |
| `println` | `println(...)` | Writes its arguments followed by a newline. |
| `range` | `range(arg, [arg], [arg])` | Creates an exclusive integer range. |
| `repr` | `repr(arg)` | Debug representation of a value (strings are quoted). |
| `sleep` | `sleep(arg)` | Blocks for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `str` | `str(arg)` | Converts a value to its string form. |
| `type` | `type(arg)` | The type name of a value. |
| `values` | `values(arg)` | Values of a map. |

| ---- | --------- | ----- |

## `net`

| Name | Signature | Notes |
| ---- | --------- | ----- |
| `accept` | `accept(arg)` | Waits for one connection, checks its hello, and returns its handle. |
| `close` | `close(arg)` | Closes a socket handle. |
| `connect` | `connect(arg, arg, [arg])` | Connects and says hello. Options: timeout, token, maxFrame. |
| `decode` | `decode(arg)` | Decodes bytes produced by encode back into a value. |
| `encode` | `encode(arg)` | Encodes a value to a list of bytes. |
| `listen` | `listen(arg, [arg], [arg])` | Listens on a port and returns a server handle. Options: token, maxFrame. |
| `maxFrame` | `maxFrame(arg, arg)` | Largest frame this socket accepts; a peer cannot make you allocate more. |
| `peer` | `peer(arg)` | Address of the other side of a connection. |
| `port` | `port(arg)` | Local port of a socket (useful after listen(0)). |
| `receive` | `receive(arg)` | Waits for one frame and returns the decoded value. |
| `receiveBytes` | `receiveBytes(arg, arg)` | Reads exactly n bytes (no frame header). |
| `send` | `send(arg, arg)` | Encodes a value and sends it as one frame. |
| `sendBytes` | `sendBytes(arg, arg)` | Sends raw bytes (no frame header). Used by protocols layered on net. |
| `timeout` | `timeout(arg, arg)` | Sets the receive/send timeout in milliseconds (0 waits forever). |
| `udpListen` | `udpListen(arg, [arg], [arg])` | Binds a UDP socket and returns its handle. Options: timeout. |
| `udpReceive` | `udpReceive(arg, [arg])` | Receives one datagram as {from, data}, or nil when a timeout expires. |
| `udpSend` | `udpSend(arg, arg, arg, arg)` | Sends one datagram: udpSend(socket, host, port, data). |
